title: Predicting postoperative pain in patients undergoing surgery for a degenerative spine disease using preoperative peak alpha frequency.
summary: Previous studies have shown that there is an association between peak alpha frequency (PAF) measured by electroencephalography (EEG) and susceptibility to severe pain after thoracotomy. The purpose of this study is to investigate this association in a group of patients undergoing spinal surgery for the treatment of back and/or neck pain and/or due to irritation/damage of a nerve root.

interventions.name:
Patients who are surgically treated for a degenerative spine
disease.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Indication for surgical treatment of a degenerative
spine disease
• The patient is able to understand the nature,
significance and scope of the clinical study in the
context of patient information and to base the
decision to participate in the study on this.
Exclusion criteria:
Age < 18 years or >80 years
• Serious internal medicine/infectious disease
• Severe psychiatric illness
• Drug, alcohol or medication abuse
